$comment: Swift<->JS public-surface parity map. Keys under `symbols` are CadenceCore selectors as check-parity.mjs extracts them (funcs and inits keyed with external labels; stored fields and enum cases are out of scope in v1, and an init that only assigns stored fields is listed `swiftOnly` for the same reason). A value is the JS export twin (string), {"js": export, "note": why-the-shape-differs}, or {"swiftOnly": reason}. `webOnly` lists JS exports with no twin in the module's Swift file; the reason names the Swift counterpart elsewhere, if there is one. Every export of `js` must be accounted for; modules that share a `js` file each list the `// ---- Section ----` headers they own in `jsSections` and account for the exports under those. A twin claimed by any module accounts for the export wherever it sits (JS sections do not follow Swift file boundaries one for one), so a module whose twins all sit in sections other modules own lists `jsSections: []`. A `webOnly` reason that names a Swift counterpart in an unmapped file becomes a twin entry when that file is mapped.
